correctness.rationale: The direct four-edge-neighbour count yields the exact equations \(r(u)+r(v)=4\) on red edges and =2 on blue edges. The exhaustive allowed endpoint-type pairs cannot connect {0,2} to {1,3}; connectivity forces one class, yielding a unique perfect code by the red-incidence-zero or red-incidence-three vertices. The converse code construction gives two same-colour and two opposite-colour neighbours for each edge. Distinct code/colour pairs give distinct colourings. Dominating set size >= \(|V(G)|/4\) and equality exactly means disjoint closed neighbourhoods. The circular-ladder case follows from the two exact zero-one neighbourhood equations. A standard-library replay independently enumerated raw colourings and codes on varied connected cubic graphs and reproduced every tested set, but finite tests are only corroboration. Unproved: indices exceeding two on code-free graphs.

originality.rationale: The verified new content is a family-uniform two-colour structural characterization and exact bijection in connected cubic graphs, not the 2026 introduction of strong-majority colouring, not classical perfect codes, and not the known \(K_4\) index-two instance. Full or substantive primary material on the 2026 general bounds and prior balanced-colouring literature was compared at the level of statements, not just titles. Neither the reported general bounds nor the special graph classifications entail the claimed universal bijection. Searches of research records and alternative terminology did not identify an identical or dominating theorem. Historical priority remains provisional; unavailable full text and uncatalogued work are residual risks.
residual_risks: A prior equivalence may exist under open-neighbourhood-balanced line-graph terminology not surfaced by the searches.
The complete manuscript of the indexed complete-graph study was not accessible; only its precise public result summary was compared, and no all-cubic coverage is inferred from that absence.
Finite verification cannot settle arbitrary graph order, and independent mathematical and historical audit has not been performed.

value.rationale: The new 2026 invariant is a local edge-colouring condition, while efficient domination is a global vertex-covering condition. An exact if-and-only-if and a canonical two-to-one count between these problems for every connected cubic graph is a natural complete structural characterization, giving a domination-equality test for the two-colour threshold, a divisibility-by-four obstruction, a transfer mechanism for enumeration/algorithms from perfect codes, and explicit nontrivial infinite examples. This is not merely a single graph, parameter substitution, or restatement of an old scalar bound. The prism instance is illustrative and its known domination count is not counted as the contribution. The broader three/four-colour problem remains unproved.
